title: Compact Playbook Bundler (OpsConDenser) and Runtime Shims
creator: Ava Thompson
description:
Problem: Our current runbooks are long, frequently redundant, and expensive to execute in support automation scenarios. Operators repeatedly run multi-step scripts that could be composed and cached, but the current tooling treats runbooks as monolithic artifacts, causing slow iteration, duplicated telemetry surface area, and brittle rollouts.

Proposal: Build OpsConDenser, a compact playbook bundler that serializes runbooks into small immutable 'compactlets' with metadata (inputs, outputs, idempotency hints, KV-cache keys, required permissions). Provide lightweight runtime shims that can: (1) validate signatures, (2) materialize required env for safe dry-runs, (3) selectively execute steps (slicing), and (4) emit structured telemetry for each compactlet step. Compactlets should be optimized for network transfer and caching in the serving runtime so on-call flows and automated remediation can run with minimal warm-up.

Scope:
- Bundler CLI service that converts annotated runbook YAML -> compactlet tarball + manifest.
- Runtime shim library (Go + Node) for embedding compactlet execution with safety guards.
- Prefix/KV caching hooks: manifest contains cache key selectors so runtime can skip repeated prep steps.
- Canary rollout mechanism: tag compactlets with rollout policy and fallback compactlets for graceful degradation.
- Audit and signature verification integration with KMS to satisfy Private deployment compliance.

Design trade-offs:
- Compactlets are immutable snapshots for reproducibility; downside: more artifacts to store and GC. We'll mitigate with TTL and delta-patching metadata.
- Signature/KMS checks add latency; we will cache verification tokens per session and allow a "fast-verify" mode for trusted internal clusters.
- To keep compactlets small, we recommend referencing large binaries via signed URIs rather than embedding them.

Non-goals: Full visual editor for playbooks (PM will scope separately), replacing existing runbook storage backends in this iteration.
acceptance_criteria: Bundler converts annotated runbook YAML into a compactlet with manifest and signs it using KMS
Runtime shim can execute a compactlet in dry-run and live modes with per-step structured telemetry
KV-prefix caching reduces average setup token count for a standard repair flow by >=30% in e2e smoke tests
Canary rollout supports tag-based rollout with automatic fallback to prior compactlet on failure
Security review completed and audit trail exists for compactlet execution (logs + signatures)
technical_notes: Compactlet manifest fields: id, version, step_hashes[], cache_keys[], required_scopes[], rollout_tags[], signature. Use xz compression and binary diff-friendly layout to enable delta updates. Runtime shims expose exec API with hooks: before_step(context), after_step(result), on_error(policy). We'll reuse existing telemetry schema from ENG-314162 and emit 'compactlet.step' events with step_index and duration. Canary controller will be implemented as a policy evaluator in the console rollout service. Garbage collection: TTL + last-used index recorded in object storage metadata.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: mass proliferation of compactlets inflates object-store costs. Mitigation: aggressive TTL policy and background dedupe by manifest hash. Risk: operator confusion with multiple compactlet versions. Mitigation: console UI will show active rollouts and auto-link runbook source. Risk: KMS throttling on signature verification. Mitigation: verification token cache and batched verification during bundling.
tasks: Spec: compactlet manifest and compression format
Implement bundler CLI + server: YAML -> compactlet
Implement Go runtime shim and adapters for operator CLI
Integrate signature/KMS verification flow and token cache
E2E smoke tests for caching and canary fallback
Console: basic rollout visibility for compactlets
